Fit XAddiVortes, the fast fit of AddiVortes

Source: R/xaddivortes.R
xaddivortes.Rd

XAddiVortes is a fast point fit of the additive ensemble of Voronoi tessellations of AddiVortes (Stone and Gosling, 2025), in place of Markov chain Monte Carlo. The columns are screened by binned mutual information with the response, and the tessellations are built in turn on the running residual with damped, shrunk cell values. Each round then replaces the share with the smallest log Bayes factor under the model's prior by fresh tessellations and refits every cell value, and a final refit chooses the damping by generalised cross-validation. The result is a single point estimate, not a posterior sample. Starting the sampler from the fit, thiessen(start = "fast"), gives posterior draws after the burn-in.

Usage

xaddivortes(x, ...)

# Default S3 method
xaddivortes(
  x,
  y,
  params = NULL,
  control = thiessen_control(),
  seed = NULL,
  threads = getOption("mc.cores", 1L),
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'data.frame'
xaddivortes(
  x,
  y,
  params = NULL,
  control = thiessen_control(),
  seed = NULL,
  threads = getOption("mc.cores", 1L),
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'formula'
xaddivortes(
  formula,
  data,
  params = NULL,
  control = thiessen_control(),
  seed = NULL,
  threads = getOption("mc.cores", 1L),
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A numeric matrix or data frame of covariates.

...

Not used; must be empty.

y

The numeric response.

params

The settings, from xaddivortes_params(); NULL takes the defaults.

control

The model configuration, from thiessen_control(); its mean_params set the number of tessellations and the covariate space. The sweep schedule is not used.

seed

The seed, as for thiessen().

threads

Threads for prediction.

formula

A formula, response ~ covariates.

data

A data frame holding the variables of formula.

Value

An object of class c("xaddivortes", "thiessen"): a thiessen() fit with one draw, the fast fit, whose noise draw is the fit's sigma, so every method of the fit uses that value. Its fast element is a list of sigma, the noise estimate on the response's scale; column_scores, the screening scores named by column; train_score, the training residual root mean square after the build, after each round and after the final refit; and seconds, the elapsed fit time.

Details

The noise estimate sigma(fit) is the root of the training residual sum of squares over the residual degrees of freedom of the final refit. Those degrees of freedom do not count the choice of the cells, so the intervals of predict(fit, interval = "prediction") can cover less than their level; vignette("fast-fits", package = "thiessen") measures the coverage on held-out data. Split-conformal intervals around the fit (Lei and others, 2018) are calibrated without that assumption: fit on one part of the data and widen the prediction by the level quantile of the absolute residuals on the other part.

The fit holds one draw, so it has no posterior to compare models by: log_lik(), and with it loo::loo() and loo::waic(), refuse it with an error of class thiessen_error.

The design and response are handled as by thiessen(): a matrix, a data frame or a formula, factors encoded as treatment-contrast indicators. The model is the Gaussian one, so the response must be numeric; a response or a control that selects another family is an error.

XAddiVortes is experimental: it needs a build with the core's experimental feature (core_experimental()) and errors with the condition class thiessen_requires_feature otherwise.

References

Lei, J., G'Sell, M., Rinaldo, A., Tibshirani, R. J. and Wasserman, L. (2018). Distribution-free predictive inference for regression. Journal of the American Statistical Association 113(523), 1094-1111. doi:10.1080/01621459.2017.1307116

Stone, A. and Gosling, J. P. (2025). AddiVortes: (Bayesian) additive Voronoi tessellations. Journal of Computational and Graphical Statistics 34(3), 859-871. doi:10.1080/10618600.2024.2414104

See also

xaddivortes_params(), thiessen(), predict.xaddivortes(), summary.xaddivortes()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # core_experimental()
set.seed(1)
x <- matrix(runif(400), ncol = 2)
y <- sin(6 * x[, 1]) + x[, 2] + rnorm(200, sd = 0.1)
control <- thiessen_control(tessellations = 20)
fit <- xaddivortes(x, y, params = xaddivortes_params(rounds = 10),
                   control = control, seed = 1)
fit

frame <- data.frame(y = y, a = x[, 1], b = x[, 2])
xaddivortes(y ~ a + b, frame, control = control, seed = 1)
}
